fix_commit.message: avcodec/bsf/dts2pts: fix binary tree invariant violation on selective dec_poc
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: In-place mutation of AVTree node keys (poc) violates binary tree sort invariant
findings.message: hevc_queue_frame() detects that a newly decoded frame has a POC that requires renumbering ('decrementing') the POC of previously-queued nodes that belong to the same GOP. To do this it calls av_tree_enumerate() with the `same_gop` comparator to walk the tree and, for every matching node, invokes `dec_poc()` via the enumerate 'cmp' callback, which directly mutates `node->poc -= dec` while the node is still linked in the AVTree keyed by (poc, gop) (see cmp_insert/dec_poc). AVTree (like any binary search tree) relies on the invariant that a node's key never changes while it remains in the tree — mutating the key in place while iterating over the tree can reorder elements relative to their siblings, break the enumeration itself (which is walking the tree using the old, now-stale ordering), and can produce two different nodes with identical (poc, gop) keys. This is exactly the class of use documented for av_tree_enumerate()/av_tree_insert(): keys must not be changed while a node is a member of the tree. On malformed/adversarial HEVC streams causing selective POC decrements (`poc < s->nb_frame && hevc->gop == s->gop`), this corrupts the tree structure and subsequent tree operations (insert/find/enumerate) can walk into invalid pointers or read past allocated bounds, which OSS-Fuzz reported as an out-of-array access (heap OOB read/corruption) in the DTS2PTS BSF fuzzer.
findings.suggestion: Do not mutate the sort key (poc) of nodes while they remain inside the AVTree. First collect pointers to all nodes matching the GOP predicate into a temporary array (without touching them), then for each collected node: remove it from the tree (or re-insert after modification using av_tree_insert with the new key), decrement its poc, and re-insert it into the tree; handle the case where the new key collides with an existing node (free/merge duplicates) instead of assuming uniqueness. This is exactly what the actual fix (054dffd13368f8d7d024dbdfdce7454e6e547c5f) implements via collect_same_gop() + a two-step remove/insert dance with collision handling.

ground_truth.root_cause: The code mutates the sort key of an AVTree node (DTS2PTSNode.poc, part of the (poc, gop) key used by cmp_insert) via av_tree_enumerate()'s callback while the node remains linked in the tree, instead of removing the node, updating it, and re-inserting it (with collision handling) as required by AVTree's usage contract.
